$comment: Test placement manifest. Which framework test suites run on which backend, tier and runner class.
.github/scripts/run-tests.sh reads this file; the lane workflows only say which tiers and backends a job covers.
Placement follows section 5.2 of the automation baseline report: a suite runs on the cheapest runner class that
satisfies its requirement. Every suite carries the reason for its tier so the port can be checked line by line.
Tiers: fast (no device), windowed (a window plus a software renderer: xvfb+Mesa on Linux, WARP on Windows),
software-gpu (Mesa llvmpipe / lavapipe; populated by the Phase C measurement pass), hardware (a real GPU or audio
device: self-hosted only), quarantine (known broken; never run, listed so it is not forgotten).
Runner classes: hosted-linux, hosted-linux-arm64, hosted-windows, hosted-macos, selfhosted-windows, selfhosted-macos.
Suite fields: id, tier, backends, reason, and one of test (NUnitLite --test), where (NUnitLite --where) or filter
(dotnet test --filter when runner is dotnet-test); optional runners (restrict to classes), skip (os or arch names),
